ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A family pedigree chart with two monogenic genetic diseases, A and B, is as follows. Disease A is a certain familial hereditary tumor, controlled by the alleles A/a; disease B is phenylketonuria, caused by a deficiency of phenylalanine hydroxylase, controlled by the alleles B/b, and the two pairs of genes are inherited independently. According to the figure, what is the mode of inheritance of disease A?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A family pedigree chart with two monogenic genetic diseases, A and B, is as follows. Disease A is a certain familial hereditary tumor, controlled by the alleles A/a; disease B is phenylketonuria, caused by a deficiency of phenylalanine hydroxylase, controlled by the alleles B/b, and the two pairs of genes are inherited independently. According to the figure, what is the mode of inheritance of disease A?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The legend shows that blank squares/circles are normal males and females, diagonal-line filling indicates males and females affected with disease A, horizontal-line filling indicates males affected with disease B, and cross filling indicates females affected with both disease A and disease B. In the pedigree, female No. 1 and male No. 2 in generation I are both filled with diagonal lines, that is, both are affected with disease A; among their offspring, female II-2 is cross-filled, that is, affected with both disease A and disease B, while female II-3 is blank and male II-5 is blank, both not affected with disease A. Both male and female individuals in the figure may show manifestations of disease A. Reasoning: If disease A were recessive inheritance, the two parents affected with disease A should both be recessive homozygotes, and all offspring should be affected with disease A, but normal individuals II-3 and II-5 appear in the figure, which is a contradiction. If it were X-linked dominant inheritance, all daughters of an affected father should be affected, but daughter II-3 in the figure is normal, which is a contradiction. If it were X-linked recessive inheritance, when both parents are affected, normal daughters should not appear among the offspring, which also contradicts II-3 being normal. After excluding these modes, combined with the facts that both males and females can be affected and affected parents can give birth to normal children, it accords with the characteristic in autosomal dominant inheritance that heterozygous affected parents give birth to normal children. Therefore disease A is an autosomal dominant genetic disease.
